title: Measuring Consensus in AI Agent Networks
abstract: arXiv:2610.24833v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As AI agents become increasingly connected through networks and take on tasks that require negotiation and joint decision-making, a systematic approach is needed to assess how their views converge and what information supports their decisions. We present an evaluation framework that treats consensus formation as the evolution of publicly stated positions toward a shared region, using accumulated communication history as context. The framework tracks position trajectories, group dispersion, and information expressed in public messages. Two case studies examine staffing decisions based on distributed facts and decisions requiring agents to reconcile duplicate information and a cancelled contract. Results from 1,872 completed runs associate sharing explanations with more accurate group decisions, while the second task reveals persistent disagreement despite accurate aggregate answers. translated_title: 测量AI智能体网络中的共识
translated_abstract: 随着AI智能体越来越多地通过网络连接起来，并承担需要谈判和联合决策的任务，目前需要一种系统化的方法来评估它们的观点如何趋同，以及哪些信息支撑着它们的决策。我们提出了一个评估框架，将共识形成视为公开表态立场向共享区域演化的过程，并将累积的沟通历史作为上下文。该框架跟踪立场轨迹、群体离散度以及公开消息中表达的信息。两个案例研究分别考察了基于分布式事实的人员配置决策，以及需要智能体协调重复信息和已取消合同的决策。1,872次完成运行的实验结果表明，分享解释与更准确的群体决策相关联，而第二项任务则揭示了尽管聚合答案是准确的，但分歧依然持续存在。成员变更实验提供了补充性的……
tldr: 该论文提出了一个将共识形成建模为公开立场演化的评估框架，通过跟踪立场轨迹、群体离散度和公开信息，发现智能体分享解释有助于提升群体决策准确性，但即使聚合答案准确，个体间仍可能存在持续分歧。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an evaluation framework that models consensus formation as the evolution of publicly stated positions, tracking position trajectories, group dispersion, and expressed information, finding that sharing explanations correlates with more accurate group decisions while persistent disagreement can remain even when aggregate answers are accurate.
